subject: Emotions
title: Emotion Regulation Strategies
description: A fast breakdown of Emotion Regulation Strategies for builders.

hook.text: A doctor tells a patient terminal news. She feels devastation but speaks calmly and clearly. That's emotion regulation.

buildup.text: James Gross found two main strategies: reappraisal (changing how you think) and suppression (hiding the expression).

discovery.text: Reappraisal works: reframing 'crisis' as 'challenge' cuts stress. Suppression backfires—it increases internal arousal.

twist.text: People who habitually suppress emotions have worse memory, higher blood pressure, and weaker relationships.

climax.text: Regulation isn't about eliminating emotion. It's choosing which emotions to have, when, and how intensely.

punchline.text: You can't control what you feel. But you can steer how you respond.

quiz.question: Which strategy is more effective: reappraisal or suppression?
